title: Simulating the natural lighting for a physical and mental Well-being in residential building in Dubai, UAE
authors: Naglaa Sami Abdelaziz Mahmoud et al., 2023
research_question: To investigate the context, analyze appropriate lighting in residential interiors in UAE, and present planning directions for interior spaces, specifically proposing new strategic lighting layouts (lighting scenes) standards to adapt with circadian rhythm for physical and mental well-being.
research_aims: To investigate the context and analyze appropriate lighting in residential interiors in UAE.
To present the planning direction of interior spaces for residential buildings in UAE.
To propose new strategic lighting layouts (lighting scenes) standards related to light in residential spaces for a healthy life in Dubai, UAE.
To simulate natural lighting diversity throughout the day to adapt with the circadian rhythm for physical and mental well-being using innovative artificial lamps.

methodology.design: Theoretical review and simulation-based design proposal. The study analyzed residential interior functions, human well-being status, and innovative lighting characteristics to propose new lighting layouts. Lighting scenes were simulated using 3Dmax and DIALux programs for a rendering proposal of an apartment in Dubai, UAE.
methodology.participants: Not applicable (simulation study, no human participants).
methodology.analysis: Comparative evaluation of proposed lighting environments with international illuminance standards and analysis of light environment effects on human biorhythms and visuality, physiological, and psychological factors.

overall_conclusions: The exact lighting illumination and light color temperature critically influence interior functionality and success.
A simulation of artificial lighting with different scenes can stimulate circadian rhythm and increase users' overall functionality, mimicking natural light variations.
Fixed lighting scenes lead to boredom and negatively affect user mentality.
Tuneable and dimmable lighting systems promote a healthy lighting environment.
The proposed lighting scenes for a residential apartment in Dubai, UAE, are relevant to the functionality and demands of each room's interior, aiming to support physical and mental well-being.
limitations: The study's proposals are based on simulation and theoretical review, requiring future validation through real-world application.
Future research needs to collect data from the application of the proposed lighting environment in home spaces to examine the proposal scenes.
Validation and analysis of the lighting environment should involve installing flexible lighting systems and measuring quantitative values of lighting and residents' satisfaction.
